title: The Toronto Purchase Treaty, No. 13 (1805)

publisher.en: Mississaugas of the Credit First Nation
publisher.fr: Mississaugas of the Credit First Nation

edition: Web page posted 3 November 2020, fetched 8 September 2026

extraction.reason: Not recorded when the page was cached, and not recovered since. What the .txt shows is a tag-stripping of the .html rather than a browser rendering: it keeps the site navigation chrome, decodes entities, holds each paragraph on one line, and carries artefacts only a regex stripper leaves - a bare `--->` where a comment opened with a `>` inside it, and a fragment of a meta attribute ending `">`. Two candidates were run on 2026-09-09 and NEITHER reproduces extractedTextSha256: a regex stripper (tags to newlines, entities decoded, blank lines dropped) and Chromium's document.body.innerText through Playwright. This is not cosmetic: content/levels/toronto.json cites this digest as the sourceHash of its territory statement, so a shipped claim is pinned to bytes that only a machine already holding the file can produce. Someone who fetched the page and matched its sha256 still cannot check the quote.

knownStaleness.topic: A nation's own account, and the reason it is cited rather than the Crown's
knownStaleness.problem: This page is the Mississaugas of the Credit's own history of the treaty their territory is defined by, which is what docs/content-review.md 3.2 asks for and what a Crown page cannot be. It is dated - posted 3 November 2020 - and the same site publishes later settlements (the Rouge Tract Settlement, 2025) that this page does not mention. Nothing cited from it here depends on the settlement record being current: the sentence used names which cities fall inside the treaty boundary.
knownStaleness.action: re-fetch before drawing any claim about settlements, compensation or claims still in progress; the boundary sentence does not move

grainNote: One web page, one heading, no pagination. The flag is on the page's settlement narrative, not on its boundary statement, because those two go stale at completely different rates and a flag covering both would fire on everything.

claimsCompared: the boundary sentence the level statement rests on: "The cities of Etobicoke, Toronto, North York, York and Vaughan are located within the boundaries of the Toronto Purchase Treaty lands."

the settlement narrative the flag covers: "In 2010, the Government of Canada settled the Toronto Purchase Claim and the Brant Tract Claim for compensation of $145 million- at that time the largest claims settlement in Canadian history."

the 1788 survey dispute: "An attempt to survey the Toronto Purchase Treaty lands in 1788 met Mississauga opposition indicating that there had been no clear delineation of land boundaries agreed upon by the Crown and the First Nation."
that this page still makes no mention of the 2025 Rouge Tract Settlement published elsewhere on the same site
the page's own stamp, which is a post date and not a modification date: "Posted on November 3, 2020"

liveChecks.consequence: Fetched first-hand, and the prose is unmoved - but THE REGISTER'S sha256 NO LONGER REPRODUCES. The live fetch is 92,809 bytes, the same length as the cache, hashing to bd8d2b37067a5c31f5e6e6ea364752be68eb8549bd33e737afaccfc4f26df9ce against this register's 585db875e61f61fd2623873462fd492e7e56670d6bac1798cf7069f1e04bb9b5. The whole of the difference is per-response WordPress state - four nonces, a Wordfence hid parameter and two plugin tokens, each a fixed-width hex string, which is why the byte count is unchanged - and nothing else; the python3 tag-stripper recorded verbatim as extraction.command in cirnac-treaty-7.json and kdfn-about-us.json, run over the live fetch and over the cached file, and the two outputs diffed produced an EMPTY diff. So extractedTextSha256 (58c92c46...), the digest content/levels/toronto.json cites as its sourceHash, still matches, and the finding is that this register's sha256 is not reproducible by re-fetching and never will be: the nonces are minted per request. Recorded rather than re-hashed, for the same reason as cirnac-algonquin-parliamentary-precinct. sourceDateModified is null because the page publishes no modification date; "Posted on November 3, 2020" is a publication date and putting it in this field would misstate what the page claims. WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO: this is a live, maintained nation website - the flag itself notes the same site published a 2025 settlement - so upstream: "does-not-revise" would be FALSE here and was not written. The chapter stays on ADR-0016 section 2 row 1 and content/levels/toronto.json's territory claim is still on an unarmed row-1 clock.
